newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks creep higher in the week.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks creep higher in the week.

text.p: Saudi Arabian shares crept higher last week with the index edging up half a percent, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index closed at 156.51 points on Thursday from 155.71 the previous week. Of the 59 companies traded in the week, 30 rose, 16 fell and 13 were unchanged.
Services sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 55 percent of volume. They were followed by industrials, with 20 percent and cement stocks, with 12 percent.
BFA put turnover in the week at 3.86 million shares worth 532.9 million riyals ($142 million) from 3.71 million shares worth 601.5 million riyals.

For the third week running Arriyadh Development was the most actively traded stock, accounting for 20 percent of volume. It also continued to chalk up gains, ending almost four percent higher at 83 riyals.
Among the week's biggest gainers were Amiantit, which gathered nearly nine percent to 61 riyals, and Tihama, which added 8.6 percent to 63 riyals.
Southern Cement was up at 472 riyals from 438. Saudi Cable was eight riyals firmer at 113.
The biggest losers in the week were Thimar, which lost 10 percent to 99 riyals and National Gypsum, which shed 27 riyals to 303 riyals.
SASCO gave up some of the previous week's gains, ending one riyal lower at 44 riyals.
